public_rationale: The funding forecast in this sentence is hedged ('all signs suggest') and open-ended, so we do not score it. The firm premise is that generative AI is 'inherently unprofitable' and that 'every single company' therefore relies on venture money. One solid counterexample defeats a claim worded this broadly. Midjourney is a leading generative AI image company. In 2022 its founder said it was 'already profitable' despite high computing costs, and that it had no investors. In August 2025 he said Midjourney would stay 'independent' and 'investor-free'. A generative AI company that turned a profit and ran for years without outside investors shows the business is not inherently unprofitable, and that not every company depends on venture funding. The premise is contradicted as stated, though it may still fit the large labs and most venture-backed startups he had in mind.
limitations: The counterexample rests on the founder's own unaudited statements, and the profit claim dates from 2022.
If 'every single company' meant only the venture-backed startups under discussion, Midjourney falls outside his scope. The premise would then be much harder to test.
One small, unusually lean company does not show that generative AI is generally profitable.

our_interpretation: The funding forecast ('all signs suggest ... must continue in perpetuity ... until everybody gives up') is hedged and open-ended, so it is not scored.

The firm, categorical part is the causal premise. Generative AI is 'inherently' unprofitable, and as a result 'every single company' depends on continued venture money ('the Silicon Valley Welfare System').

Plain reading: no generative AI company can run profitably without ongoing outside investor funding. One credible example of a generative AI company that was profitable and self-funded contradicts both 'inherently' and 'every single company'.

'Inherently' is a claim about the technology's nature, not one quarter. So the period is the commercial generative AI era up to the post, 2022 through 2025-12-29. That choice is noted in the ambiguity flags.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence shows that every generative AI company, without exception, was unprofitable and kept going only on repeated outside funding during 2022–2025.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible evidence shows at least one generative AI company that was profitable and funded itself without venture or other outside investors during 2022–2025.
